evidence_quotes.quote: Diante da dificuldade de fornecer acesso adequado ao esgotamento sanitário em regiões não atendidas por sistemas centralizados, a adoção de sistemas descentralizados mostra-se relevante para a superação do déficit.
Por fim, foi realizada uma análise documental do marco legal e institucional que regulamenta o saneamento brasileiro e suas interfaces com a gestão descentralizada de esgotos.
A Lei Federal nº 11.445/2007 determina que, na ausência de redes públicas de saneamento, soluções individuais de afastamento e tratamento de esgotos são admitidas.
Após a busca, foram selecionados 36 artigos que abordavam o uso de sistemas centralizados e descentralizados.

A consulta das legislações vigentes foi realizada respeitando-se a hierarquia legal, com a avaliação das diretrizes constitucionais e, em seguida, das infraconstitucionais (leis, decretos, atos normativos, portarias e resoluções). Como critério de avaliação das legislações, somente documentos em vigência no ano de 2019 foram avaliados.

Verificou-se, ainda, que entre as alternativas tecnológicas utilizadas em ETEs de pequeno porte no Brasil, os TS+FAN e os reatores UASB apresentam destaque. Três estados brasileiros, localizados no Sudeste e Sul, possuem leis que determinam a utilização de TS+FAN na ausência de redes coletivas de coleta.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines decentralized household (onsite/individual) and community (cluster) sewage solutions in Brazil conceptually and doctrinally as an approach to addressing the sanitation service deficit in rural, peri-urban, and unserved areas.
criterion_notes.c2: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, this clearly qualifies (plain=yes) because it conducts a documentary analysis of Brazilian federal and state sanitation laws, decrees, and regulations governing decentralized sewage management. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it doctrinally discusses regulatory structure and statutory rules allocating public-service responsibility vs. private owner responsibility for sanitation provision and operation in unserved, rural, and low-income/ZEIS areas (e.g., Lei 11.445/2007, Lei 14.026/2020, Decreto 7.217/2010, Santa Catarina Lei 17.492/2018, Maranhão Lei 9.550/2012), alongside operational/environmental rules on effluent standards and GPS tracking of septic-sludge trucks. Under both the plain and narrow readings, however, the paper fails Criteria 3 and 4 and is excluded as E05.
criterion_notes.c3: No empirical evidence on service access and not a systematic empirical synthesis. The paper combines (1) a narrative literature review of 36 engineering/management papers and manuals on conceptual pros/cons of centralized vs. decentralized wastewater treatment, (2) a doctrinal/documentary review of federal and state statutes in force in 2019, and (3) a secondary descriptive breakdown of engineering treatment technologies (e.g., UASB reactors, septic tanks + anaerobic filters) across operating urban sewage treatment plants from ANA (2017). It explicitly notes on p. 49 that empirical impacts of recent legal changes cannot yet be analyzed and collects no primary or secondary empirical data linking governance/legal rules to sanitation access.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports no empirical outcome measuring household or community sanitation access, connection, service availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion. National coverage figures from Plansab (2013) and PSBR (2019) are cited only as background context, while Results report only conceptual pros/cons (Table 1), statutory provisions (Tables 2 and 4), ABNT technical treatment efficiencies (Table 3), and the percentage distribution of treatment technologies across small sewage treatment plants (Figure 2).
criterion_notes.c5: No empirical study population, exposure-outcome analysis, or empirical study design assessing service access; the paper is a narrative/conceptual review and doctrinal regulatory overview with descriptive engineering technology counts.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in Portuguese, which is an eligible language without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Narrative literature review, doctrinal/documentary legal analysis, and descriptive secondary inventory of sewage treatment plant technologies
population_and_sample: 36 literature articles on centralized/decentralized wastewater management, Brazilian federal and state sanitation laws in force in 2019, and secondary inventory of small sewage treatment plants from ANA (2017) (no empirical household or community access sample)
exposure: Federal and state legal/regulatory provisions governing decentralized sewage systems and wastewater treatment technological alternatives (doctrinal and conceptual review only)
outcome: Descriptive distribution of treatment technologies in small urban sewage treatment plants (ANA 2017) and doctrinal inventory of federal/state laws; no empirical sanitation access outcome reported
rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). Although the paper is in Portuguese (c6=yes), discusses decentralized sanitation solutions for unserved rural, peri-urban, and low-income areas in Brazil (c1=yes), and doctrinally reviews federal and state sanitation laws defining public-service vs. private responsibility for decentralized sewage treatment and sludge management (c2=yes), it contains no empirical evidence on sanitation service access and is not a systematic empirical synthesis (c3=no). Instead, it combines a narrative literature review of centralized vs. decentralized wastewater treatment, a doctrinal/documentary inventory of Brazilian legislation, and a descriptive summary of treatment technologies used in small sewage treatment plants from ANA (2017), without reporting any empirical household or community access outcome (c4=no, c5=no). Both the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 decision and the plain Criterion 2 decision are exclude.
